ranking.note: Moved up relative to other P3s because it guards the cluster mempool project, which this category ranks above generic policy conveniences.

inconsistencies: #35882 and #36214 are both test-only additions but sit in different bands; this is deliberate: #36214 exercises cluster mempool trimming during reorgs (a category-defining project), while #35882 only asserts an exact reject string for already-rejected Taproot spends.

#29247 (OP_CAT) and #36122 (BIP460 CISA) are both soft-fork reference implementations whose mempool footprint is limited to standardness/discouragement; they are kept at the same band. The substantive review load for both lies in consensus/script, not in this category, so neither should displace #35286/#36214 here.

#36182 and #35026 are the only two PRs fixing behaviour users actually feel (fee underbidding on startup/sparse mempool; false eviction of valid BIP68 transactions after a reorg); they should be reviewed before any of the policy-extension or test PRs. #36182 first, since the failure mode (severe fee underestimation reported downstream by LDK) is ongoing in production.

#35923 (unbroadcast txid memory accounting) overlaps conceptually with mempool limit enforcement but is self-described as ~80 bytes per transaction; it has no claim on review time ahead of #35026 despite both being labelled bug fixes.
result.notes: Two clear P2 bug fixes, a middle block of P3 policy/feature/test work, and a P4 tail of narrow test and cleanup items; no band changes were needed, the list already used the range sensibly. Note that a large fraction of the reviewer effort implied by #29247 and #36122 falls outside this category.
